value.rationale: The split-versus-cherry relationship is a natural structural dependence question for uniform random trees. The theorem identifies the exact first internal-node size at which an inward root-split change cannot be analyzed by any all-threshold stochastic dominance, establishes an infinite family of this failure, and distinguishes such distributional comparisons from known conditional mean signs. This supplies a sharp boundary for interpreting cherry-count tail tests and avoids arbitrary parameter slicing.
